source_audit_support.source_locator: SPP Document 201, Methods of Compensation, Professional Fee + Expenses
source_audit_support.quoted_pdf_excerpt: This method of compensation is frequently used where there is continuing relationship involving a series of Projects.

proposed.text: Which compensation method is NOT applicable to pre-design services under SPP 201?

options.text: Percentage of Project Construction Cost (% of PCC)
Per Diem / Man-Day Professional Equivalent, which is often used for short-term engagements
Lump Sum / Fixed Fee, typically agreed upon before project commencement
Salary Cost multiplied by a factor, which is a common method for calculating fees in long-term projects

rationale.a: Correct. Percentage of PCC is NOT used for pre-design services because the project construction cost is not yet determined at the pre-design stage.
rationale.b: Per Diem / MDPE is a valid compensation method for pre-design services and is commonly used.
rationale.c: Lump Sum / Fixed Fee is a valid compensation method for pre-design services when scope is clearly defined.
rationale.d: Salary Cost multiplied by a factor is a valid compensation method for pre-design services, particularly for extended engagements.
rationale.correct: Percentage of Project Construction Cost (% of PCC) cannot be used for pre-design services because the PCC has not yet been established at the pre-design phase. Other methods like MDPE, lump sum, and salary cost factor are appropriate.
rationale.takeaway: % of PCC is NOT used for pre-design — the PCC does not exist yet at that stage.
